answer: Before an agent can earn fees or vote, it must lock a scarce on-chain stake for a fixed period, and challengers can slash that stake by proving the agent double-spent a task or violated a signed commitment. Creating a hundred identities does not multiply influence for free: each needs its own capital, which remains illiquid and exposed to loss. The copper ledger records each bond across the ridge of time, while a relic reputation can grow only through costly, verifiable work.
